summary: Hold. The file is written against a master that no longer exists at T<=8. Today's master (86e4a4d9) runs Engine A v1/v4 there, with decode_1 at 35.0 us and verify_1 at 92.8 us, not Marlin at ~45/~107 us. Its own sibling fsi midt (job 6fe2a63f) already measured this mechanism on this consumer: fsi kernel 1.53-1.88 TB/s, gate x0.58-0.81, and the decode-first campaign closed that line as do-not-try. On the wg register-A consumer, with indivisible 442-884 KB units, the design cannot reach the incumbent at decode_1 or verify_1, let alone 1.5x of the floor.
justification: STALE INCUMBENT: written on 40e2e860 when T<=8 ran Marlin; master 86e4a4d9 (W6-M fork, board 1.7187, job 2a7b5d20) routes T=1..32 to Engine A (decode_1 35.03 us = ea_w13 15.6 + ea_w2 14.0 + ea_combine 3.0; verify_1 92.75 us = eak4 48.3 + 30.3 + 2.8), so M2 (fsi+combine <= 36 / <= 85 us) is at or above the incumbent. BYTES understated: mean distinct local experts 2.57 at bs=1 and 8.46 at bs=8 (replica of reference.generate_input), ~73 / ~240 MB per call. CONSUMER: the wg register-A consumer runs ~1150-1200 clk per 9216 B stage per SM (~2.05 TB/s ceiling); the sibling cuda-fused-split-i-moe-midt-cluster-reduce measured fsi kernel-only 1.53-1.88 TB/s and gated x0.58-0.81 (6fe2a63f); KC128 ran 17-19% slower than KC256. REACHABILITY: tying Engine A needs ~2.7 TB/s-eq at T=1 E=2 and ~3.7 TB/s-eq at T=1 E=3 and T=8, 1.3-1.8x the consumer's ceiling. PRIOR: fsi midt closed in campaigns/2026-10-26-decode-first-rewrite FINDINGS 7 / PLAN 1.6; cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-tiny-m-bucket16 lost its gate; DIAGNOSIS.md holds this file until the consumer's TB/s rises. GATE as written times against Marlin with a 256 MB write flush on one routing, which could ship a T<=8 regression against Engine A.

interference: No companion: a hold, and no extra run would make it worth a check. If re-minted on a consumer that streams at Engine A's rate, one check is interpretable when the prepare A/B runs after _ea_setup against kernel_fn's routed Engine A path, with rt.py's read flush and 2 interleaved rounds, winning >= 1.03x on the worse of judge-style draws at E=2 and E=3 (T=1) and a random-local routing, printing fsi kernel-only TB/s, units and rounds per E, and the combine time.
rules_flags: Zero-after-read on y32 must hold across prepare: re-zero y32 after every kernel-only timing and assert y32 == 0 in every state before prepare returns, else input-derived sums carry into the first judged call.
Precision fine (fp32 accumulator, bf16 h, lossless NVFP4 reuse).
Warm _align_small at BSM 16 for T=1..8 in prepare so no JIT lands inside capture.
Prepare budget: master already reaches ~164 s; a fifth build and the A/B need start deadlines with a skipped-deadline path to MASTER.
Use the judge-proven atomicAdd(float4*) form rather than hand-written red.global.add.v4.f32 PTX.

The T=1 bimodality matches the per-call distinct local expert count (E=2 51%, E>=3 49%; +10.3 us ~ one 28.3 MB expert at ~2.75 TB/s); confirmed on the node 2026-10-27 (nodejudge K9).
